title: Rising Prices Become a Big Issue in the US Midterm Elections
summary:
Americans will vote in the midterm elections on November 3, less than three weeks away. These elections decide who controls the US Congress. Polls suggest that rising prices are on many voters' minds.

For nearly a year, President Donald Trump has tried to convince voters not to worry about prices. He has called concerns about affordability a "con job by Democrats." He has also said that gas and diesel prices, which rose sharply after the war with Iran began, would start falling soon. CBC News reported that Trump said consumer prices had fallen during his term, when they had actually risen.

Many voters do not seem convinced. On average, more than 70 percent of people in recent polls disapprove of how Trump has handled inflation, according to Silver Bulletin, which combines results from many polls. Inflation means prices going up over time.

New government data released on Wednesday showed that prices in September were 3.7 percent higher than a year earlier. Much of that rise came from fuel and clothing.

Spencer Kimball leads the Emerson College Polling Center in Boston. He said the economy is the top issue for voters, and that the cost of everyday things, rather than jobs or taxes, is driving their concerns. "It looks like it's just everyday expenses that are beginning to pile up," he told CBC News.

Trump has recently traveled to states such as Alaska, Kansas, Ohio and Texas to support Republican candidates for the US Senate. He won all of those states easily in 2024. Tim Malloy, a polling analyst at Quinnipiac University, called the trips "a last mad dash" to help Republican candidates who are now at risk largely because of cost-of-living worries.
why_it_matters: Which party controls Congress affects the laws that are passed, and rising prices shape what families can afford every day.

keywords.explanation: US elections held halfway through a president's four-year term, mainly to choose members of Congress.

How easy or hard it is for people to pay for the things they need.
A general rise in prices over time, so the same money buys less.

background_read: In the United States, midterm elections happen between presidential elections, and voters choose members of the House of Representatives and about a third of the Senate.
Whichever party wins more seats controls Congress, which writes laws and can support or block a president's plans.
Inflation is measured by tracking the prices of common goods, such as fuel and clothing, and comparing them with a year earlier.
Polling groups ask many people the same questions so they can estimate what voters across the country think.
